result:
To eliminate the psychological distance between an action and its consequence—specifically, to make empathy visceral and unavoidable.

Most of the world’s destructive systems don't run on pure malice; they run on abstraction. It is easy to authorize a war, exploit labor, degrade an ecosystem, or ignore suffering when the human cost is reduced to statistics, quarterly targets, or ideological labels. The people who make large-scale decisions rarely have to feel the fear, hunger, or despair of the people who absorb the impact.

If every person instantly and involuntarily experienced the exact physical and emotional reality of the harm their choices inflicted on others, cruelty and negligence would become impossible to sustain. Oppression would feel like self-harm. 

Almost every crisis—war, systemic poverty, ecological collapse—is a downstream symptom of the ability to look away. If no one could look away, the solutions would follow naturally.
